title: Game Day Plan — Incident Bot Collectors (Deploy + Config Diff + Saturation)
linked_artifacts: Slack: #incidents thread 1707764888_452019 (partial failure due to metrics lag)
content:
Doc purpose
- Validate incident bot “context bundles” are useful in the first 2–5 minutes of triage, under realistic load and failure modes.
- Exercise: deploy collector, config diff collector, saturation snapshot collector, and bundle assembly + Slack formatting.
- Confirm guardrails: timeouts, fail-open behavior, redaction + restricted-mode posting, and bounded load.

Scope (what we will test)
- Bundle assembly order + readability in Slack incident threads (#incidents)
- Collector correctness for region/service scoping
- “Suspected change” heuristic behavior (must not overclaim)
- Fail-open behavior (partial bundle + clear error sections)
- Restricted-mode behavior for sensitive incidents (minimal metadata in #incidents; full bundle in restricted channel)
- Observability + metrics emitted by bot (latency, collector error rates, cache hit rate)

Out of scope for game day
- Auto-mitigation (bot executing rollbacks / config changes)
- Broad GA rollout

Date/time
- Proposed window: 2025-02-26 18:00–19:30 UTC (60–90 min)
- Backup window: 2025-02-27 18:00–19:30 UTC
- Channels:
  - Primary coordination: #eng-sre
  - Live exercise: #incidents (use “GAME-DAY” naming)
  - Restricted-mode validation: #incidents-restricted (if available) or designated restricted channel (per security allowlist)

Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): Sean Gallagher
- Game-day facilitator / timekeeper: Talia Benson
- Bot operator (feature flags / toggles): Jacob Stein
- Observability lead (dashboards + alert correlations): Allison Grant
- Telemetry plumbing support (metrics backend / lag simulation): Logan Wright
- Platform/config support (routing snapshots + diffs): Priya Natarajan (backup: Benji Okafor)
- Release metadata support (deploy annotation events / schema): Connor O'Brien (backup: Devon Price)
- Security observer (restricted mode + redaction spot checks): Marcus Lin
- Multi-region correctness observer: Miles Thornton
- Metrics/toil measurement: Aisha Bello

Pre-req checklist (must be done 24h prior)
1) Feature flags
- Confirm bot collectors enabled in beta mode only for game-day channel(s).
- Confirm per-channel allowlist is enforced.
- Confirm “restricted mode” toggle available and tested in staging.

2) Data sources ready
- Deploy event stream has recent test deploys in at least 2 regions (us-east, eu-west).
- Config snapshot endpoint responds within SLO for “effective routing policy” by region.
- Saturation dashboards exist and have canonical links for the services used.

3) Safety
- Use synthetic / non-customer traffic for inducing errors/latency.
- Any config changes must be in staging OR in an isolated canary service with explicit rollback plan.
- Validate no customer payloads/tokens can appear in bot output (redaction enforced).

4) Logging / evidence
- Ensure bot emits per-collector timing + status metrics.
- Ensure Slack permalink capture is working (we’ll paste permalinks into feedback section).

5) Confirm “game-day services”
- Use a dedicated test service name for clarity (proposal): inference-gateway-canary (or existing internal canary service).
- Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1 (add ap-southeast-1 only if time permits).

Success criteria (what “pass” looks like)
- Speed: First context bundle lands in incident thread within 120 seconds of incident creation (p95 during game day).
- Usefulness: Responders can identify likely suspect change (deploy/config) or saturation within 5 minutes WITHOUT asking for additional context.
- Correctness:
  - Deploy collector shows correct service/region mapping and includes PR/release links.
  - Config diff collector compares (t-30m vs now) correctly, includes only allowlisted keys, and labels redacted fields clearly.
  - Saturation collector points to correct region dashboards and uses standard metric names.
- Reliability:
  - If any collector fails, bundle posts anyway with a clearly labeled partial section (“collector timed out / metrics delayed”).
  - Collector timeouts are respected (no long stalls in Slack posting).
- Noise control:
  - Bot posts at most 1 bundle automatically per incident phase, with follow-up only on explicit request / command.
  - Formatting fits within reasonable Slack block length; noisy sections are collapsed or summarized.
- Security:
  - In restricted-mode, public channel gets minimal safe summary (no customer identifiers), full detail goes only to restricted channel.
  - Redaction audit log entry created for the incident bundle (spot-check 2 cases).

Metrics to capture during game day
- Time-to-first-bundle (TTFB) and per-collector latency
- Collector error rate + reason codes (timeout, 404, metrics delayed, permission)
- Bundle completeness (% collectors succeeded)
- Cache hit rate for repeated incident updates
- “Time-to-suspect-change” (manual estimate by observers): time until someone says “likely caused by deploy X or config Y”
- Qualitative usefulness score from responders (1–5) + notes

Run of show (90 minutes)
0) (T-10 min) Setup
- Jacob: enable game-day flags for channel allowlist.
- Allison/Logan: open dashboards for deploy annotations + saturation.
- Sean: confirm comms template ready.

1) (0:00–0:10) Kickoff + guardrails
- IC assigns roles.
- Confirm rollback owners and “stop” conditions.
- Post in #eng-sre: “Game day starting; all changes are synthetic; do not page external teams.”

2) (0:10–0:25) Scenario A — Deploy regression correlation
Goal: Validate deploy collector + suspected change heuristic.
Steps
- Trigger: perform a canary deploy (or emit a test deploy annotation event) in us-east-1 for inference-gateway-canary.
- Immediately induce synthetic latency regression (e.g., increased token processing delay) in us-east-1 only.
Expected bot output
- Deploy collector shows last 2 deploys, highlights the most recent one, includes links to PR + release run.
- “Suspected change” section indicates overlap with degradation window (careful language: “possible correlation”).
Success checks
- Responders can find deploy ID + link within the posted bundle.
- No wrong-region deploy is shown.

3) (0:25–0:45) Scenario B — Config diff (routing policy) regression + redaction
Goal: Validate config diff collector accuracy + safe posting.
Steps
- Trigger: change routing policy/feature flag in eu-west-1 only (e.g., shift traffic weight to a different model variant or toggle an autoscaling knob).
- Induce synthetic error spike (5xx) in eu-west-1.
Expected bot output
- Config diff collector shows effective config at t-30m vs now, includes a concise summary (top 3 diffs), and links to config source.
- Any sensitive keys are redacted with explicit markers (e.g., “REDACTED (restricted key)”).
Success checks
- Diffs are region-scoped; no leakage of eu-west config into us-east summary.
- No customer identifiers/payloads appear.

4) (0:45–1:05) Scenario C — Saturation / throttling (429) + dashboards
Goal: Validate saturation snapshot and linkouts.
Steps
- Trigger: create synthetic load to drive queue depth and throttling (rate limit or constrained capacity) for a controlled period.
- Optional: cause KV cache pressure via long context requests (synthetic) if safe.
Expected bot output
- Saturation collector posts: GPU queue depth, throttling rate, scheduler contention (as available), with “last updated” timestamps.
- Includes canonical dashboard links for the service/region.
Success checks
- Labels match standard (per saturation-signals-standard).
- Links open and show matching time range.

5) (1:05–1:20) Scenario D — Failure mode: metrics lag / partial bundle rendering
Goal: Validate fail-open and error messaging.
Steps
- Simulate delayed metrics response (Logan to throttle metrics backend query or point collector to delayed source in staging).
Expected bot output
- Bundle posts with saturation section marked as delayed/unavailable; includes retry hint or “check dashboard link” guidance.
- Other collectors succeed and are still posted.
Success checks
- Bot does not spam retries.
- Responders understand what is missing and why.

6) (1:20–1:30) Scenario E — Restricted-mode posting (security)
Goal: Validate restricted incident handling.
Steps
- Create an incident with restricted-mode enabled.
Expected bot output
- #incidents: minimal safe bundle (no sensitive fields).
- Restricted channel: full bundle.
- Audit log entry exists.
Success checks
- No restricted content in public channel.
- Channel allowlist enforced.

Stop conditions (abort / rollback triggers)
- Any sign of customer-impacting change or spillover to production.
- Any bot output contains sensitive/customer data.
- Sustained high load caused by collectors (observed via bot metrics or metrics backend alarms).
- Bot posts repeatedly/spams or destabilizes #incidents workflow.

Scenario notes (who does what)
- Priya: config change mechanics + rollback steps; verify snapshot correctness.
- Connor/Devon: deploy event payload sanity (service naming, region tags), verify links.
- Allison/Logan: confirm dashboards correlate with what bot posts.
- Miles: verify region/time synchronization and multi-region correctness.
- Marcus: spot-check redaction and restricted mode.

How we will record feedback (during + after)
During game day
- Use a single Slack thread in #eng-sre titled: “GAME-DAY: incident bot collectors feedback (2025-02-26)”
- For each scenario, paste:
  - Incident Slack permalink(s)
  - Bot bundle permalink(s)
  - Quick rating: Useful / Neutral / Not useful
  - Notes: missing context, confusing wording, wrong links, any redaction concerns
- Aisha will keep a lightweight timeline:
  - incident start time
  - time bot posted first bundle
  - time someone identified suspected deploy/config/saturation

After game day (within 48h)
- Talia creates a short write-up section at bottom of this doc:
  - What worked
  - What didn’t
  - Top 5 action items
  - Owners + target dates
- File Linear issues (or update existing) with links:
  - ENG-2842 deploy collector follow-ups
  - ENG-2843 config diff follow-ups
  - ENG-2844 saturation collector follow-ups
  - ENG-2845 reliability hardening
  - ENG-2847 posting controls / restricted mode
  - ENG-2849 integration tests / fixtures updates

Open questions (to resolve before kickoff)
- Default time window for deploy collector in game day: last 2 deploys or last 60 minutes? (see on-call noise discussion in #eng-oncall 1707059911_552901)
- Config diff allowlist: final list of keys safe for non-restricted incidents (Marcus to confirm)
- What exact command triggers “post deeper diagnostics” (if supported) and where it is documented (PR/docs link)
- Canonical dashboard URL format: confirm stable deep links per service/region

Appendix — Comms templates
Template: #incidents incident title
- “GAME-DAY — Synthetic incident for incident-bot validation (no customer impact).”

Template: Bot usefulness vote
- “Bot bundle: Useful / Neutral / Not useful. Missing: ____. Confusing: ____. Wrong: ____.”
